source.title: Some Open Problems in the Theory of Computation as Questions about Two-Way Deterministic Pushdown Automaton Languages

accepted.question_text: For every space bound S(n) with S(n) at least log n, is the class DSPACE(S(n)) of languages accepted by deterministic Turing machines using O(S(n)) work tape space equal to the class NSPACE(S(n)) accepted by nondeterministic Turing machines using O(S(n)) work tape space? In particular, does this hold in the special case S(n)=n, the linear-bounded-automaton (LBA) case?

evidence.quote: 1. Is DSPACE(S(n)) = NSPACE(S(n)) for all S(n) >_ logn ?2 The special case S(n) = n is called "the LBA problem" and has been studied for over ten years

accepted.question_text: Is the polynomial-time class P-TIME equal to the nondeterministic polynomial-time class NP-TIME? Equivalently, does every language decidable by a nondeterministic Turing machine in polynomial time also admit a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm?
Is the class P-TIME of polynomial-time decidable languages equal to the class P-SPACE of languages decidable by deterministic Turing machines using polynomial space?
Is the polynomial-time class P-TIME equal to DLOG, the class DSPACE(log n) of languages decidable by deterministic logarithmic-space Turing machines?
Does every language in P-TIME admit a deterministic algorithm using at most O((log n)^i) space for some fixed exponent i? That is, is P-TIME contained in DSPACE((log n)^i) for some i?

evidence.quote: 5. Is P-TIME ~ DSPACE ((logn) i) for some i?

accepted.question_text: For every space bound S(n) greater than log n, does giving a space-bounded Turing machine an auxiliary pushdown stack fail to increase its computational power? Equivalently, is the class PDM(S(n)) of languages accepted by pushdown-stack Turing machines using O(S(n)) counted work-tape space equal to DSPACE(S(n))?

evidence.quote: 6. Is PDM(S(n)) = DSPACE(S(n)) for all S(n) > logn?

accepted.question_text: Is P-TIME closed under nonerasing homomorphism, meaning that applying any homomorphism that never maps a symbol to the empty string to a polynomial-time language always yields another polynomial-time language?

evidence.quote: In [2] this question is reduced to the questions: "IsP-TIME closed under nonerasing homomorphism ?" and "Is N TIME(n) ~_ P- TIME ?"

accepted.question_text: Is every language decidable by a nondeterministic Turing machine in linear time, that is every language in NTIME(n), also decidable in deterministic polynomial time, so that NTIME(n) is a subset of P-TIME?

evidence.quote: In [2] this question is reduced to the questions: "IsP-TIME closed under nonerasing homomorphism ?" and "Is N TIME(n) ~_ P- TIME ?"

accepted.question_text: Is the class 2DPDA of languages accepted by one-head two-way deterministic pushdown automata exactly equal to DLBA, the class of languages accepted by deterministic linear bounded automata?
Is the class 2DPDA of two-way deterministic pushdown automaton languages equal to the class 2DC of two-way deterministic counter-machine languages?
Is the class 2DC of languages accepted by two-way deterministic counter machines equal to the class 2NC accepted by two-way nondeterministic counter machines?
What exact inclusion or equality relationship holds between 2NC, the class of two-way nondeterministic counter-machine languages, and DLOG, the class of deterministic logarithmic-space languages?

evidence.quote: 4. What is the relationship between 2NC and DLOG?

accepted.question_text: What exact inclusion or equality relationship holds between 2DPDA, the class of two-way deterministic pushdown automaton languages, and DLOG, the class of deterministic logarithmic-space languages?

evidence.quote: 5. What is the relationship between 2DPDA and DLOG?

accepted.question_text: Is the class 2NPDA of languages accepted by two-way nondeterministic pushdown automata equal to the class 2DPDA accepted by two-way deterministic pushdown automata?

evidence.quote: A very important question--namely "is 2NPDA = 2DPDA ?"--is missing. We could not relate it to any of the open problems.

accepted.question_text: Given a language L that is already known to be accepted by a two-way deterministic pushdown automaton, or by a one-way nondeterministic counter machine, can one decide whether L also belongs to DLOG, the deterministic logarithmic-space class?
accepted.context_brief: membership of structured languages in DLOG

evidence.quote: (1) Does a given 2dpda-language (lnc-language), L, belong to DLOG?

accepted.question_text: Given a family of languages of the kind constructed in the paper, does at least one language in that family belong to 2DPDA, the class of two-way deterministic pushdown automaton languages?
accepted.context_brief: existence of a 2DPDA member in a family

evidence.quote: (2) Does one of a given family of languages belong to 2DPDA ?

accepted.question_text: Given a family consisting of 2dpda-languages or 2nc-languages of the kind constructed in the paper, does at least one language in that family belong to 2DC, the class of two-way deterministic counter-machine languages?
accepted.context_brief: existence of a 2DC member in a family

evidence.quote: (3) Does one of a family of 2dpda-languages (2no-languages) belong to 2DC?

trace.notes: Resolved the zbMATH landing page through DOI 10.1007/BF01683273 to a readable Springer PDF and mapped the main question-bearing sections: Section 1 on pages 213-214, Section 2 on page 216, and the conclusion summary on page 227.
Extracted the six headline open problems from Section 1, plus the two explicit reduced questions attached to Problem 2.
Extracted the five numbered unsolved questions about pushdown automaton and counter-machine language classes and the additional explicitly flagged missing question about 2NPDA versus 2DPDA.
Extracted the three summary decision problems listed in the conclusion because the paper presents them as open questions whose solution would settle the six problems from Section 1.
